title: Tenali Raman Tale 78 (मराठी)
summary: While inspecting the royal gardens, King Krishnadevaraya dropped his heavy gold signet ring down an ancient, narrow stone well. The well ... [MR]
full_text:
While inspecting the royal gardens, King Krishnadevaraya dropped his heavy gold signet ring down an ancient, narrow stone well. The well was fifty cubits deep, narrow as an arm, and the bottom was filled with jagged rocks and cold water.
The royal divers shook their heads:
'Maharaj, the shaft is too narrow for any man or boy to descend without suffocating, and long iron hooks cannot locate a tiny ring among the jagged rocks.'

The King turned to Tenali: 'Tenali, canst thou recover my ring without breaking the well stone or sending a man down?'

Tenali replied: 'Easily, Your Majesty! Grant me two hours, a coil of string, and a small copper bowl.'

Tenali procured a small, flat brass bowl and punched a tiny hole in its base.
He then took an enormous round bronze mirror, mounted on a wooden frame, and placed it at the top of the well at an angle that captured the midday sun, directing a concentrated beam of brilliant sunlight straight down the dark, fifty-foot shaft!
The dark depths of the well were instantly illuminated with crystal clarity!
At the bottom, resting upon a flat white river rock, the King's gold signet ring sparkled in the reflected beam of sunlight!

Tenali then smeared the bottom of the brass bowl with a thick, sticky layer of tree-resin and natural pitch (*dammar*).
He tied four strong silk cords to the rim of the bowl and lowered it carefully down the illuminated shaft using the reflected sunbeam as his guide.
Looking down the sunlit well, Tenali maneuvered the cords until the sticky bottom of the bowl rested directly upon the gold ring!

Tenali waited three minutes for the pitch to bond with the metal.
Then he gently pulled the cords upward:
Up came the brass bowl, with the King’s heavy gold signet ring firmly glued to the pitch!

Tenali cleaned the resin with warm oil and handed the sparkling ring to the King!

King Krishnadevaraya and his engineers were awestruck by Tenali’s brilliant synthesis of optics and mechanics:
'Tenali, while my divers thought of swimming, thou didst use the sun as a lantern and tree pitch as a hand!'
The King rewarded Tenali with a purse of gold coins, proving that scientific observation outshines brute force.
moral: Resourceful reflection solves puzzles where dangerous diving only stirs up mud. [MR]
